implementationDetails.audioStrategy: One AudioContext, one destination connection, for the whole instrument. Seven playable layers — Organ A/B, Piano A/B, Synth A/B/C — each build voices into a layer voice bus that runs through the documented six-unit chain (Mod 1 -> Mod 2 -> Delay -> Amp Sim/EQ -> Compressor -> Reverb) and a level fader, then into that section's bus or into the one shared Rotary Speaker. The three section buses and the rotary all meet at the master gain, which feeds a wave-shaper limiter and then the single destination; nothing bypasses that path. Piano: Grand, Upright and Electric play bundled recordings (71 mono 16-bit PCM WAV files, 24 kHz, 9.26 MB, under public/samples/); Clav, Digital and Misc are live oscillator synthesis, as is the labelled fallback voice. Organ: live additive synthesis — one oscillator per drawbar the model reads, plus generated noise-buffer transients for key click and pipe chiff, a delay-line vibrato/chorus stage, and one shared chain for both layers. Synth: live synthesis — oscillator stacks (single oscillator, sawtooth-through-shaper pulses, looped generated noise, looped generated single-cycle sync wavetables, detuned stacks, and a 2-operator FM pair), a biquad filter stack with an optional wave-shaper drive, three envelopes, an LFO and a vibrato LFO per layer, and an independent chain per layer. Organ and Synth layers are built the first time their section is switched on, so a piano-only program costs exactly the nodes Phase 2 cost. A keyboard-zone gain per note routes splits and applies crossfades before the voice is built.
